root_cause.text: nf_conntrack_helper_unregister passes NULL instead of the helper pointer to nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy, so the expectation cleanup callback never matches any expectation, leaving them dangling and causing a use-after-free when the freed helper is later dereferenced.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "nf_conntrack_helper_unregister() calls nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy() to remove expectations belonging to the helper being unregistered. However, it passes NULL instead of the helper pointer as the data argument, so expect_iter_me() never matches any expectation and all of them survive the cleanup." The patch changes the argument from NULL to `me`. The KASAN trace shows a use-after-free read in `string+0x38f/0x430` (likely accessing the helper name) after the helper is freed by `nfnl_cthelper_del`.

vuln_statements.explanation: The critical vulnerable statement: passing NULL as the second argument to nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy causes the expectation cleanup callback to never match any expectation, leaving them dangling and leading to use-after-free when the freed helper is later dereferenced.
This function definition is the entry point for helper unregister; the vulnerability is introduced inside this function by the incorrect call to nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy.
The mutex lock is taken before the vulnerable call; while not directly vulnerable, it is part of the sequence that fails to properly clean up expectations.
Removing the helper from the list without destroying its expectations creates the dangling state; the vulnerability is the missing expectation cleanup.

This is the callback function used by nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy; it is correct but the vulnerability lies in passing NULL instead of the helper pointer, so the callback is never invoked with the correct data.
